grade_and_subject.standards_system_name: Florida's State Academic Standards – Social Studies

domains.domain_name: American History - Historical Inquiry and Analysis

standards.text: Examine primary and secondary sources.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Utilize the media center, technology, or other informational sources to locate information that provides answers to questions about a historical topic.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Recognize that Native Americans were the first inhabitants in North America.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Compare the cultures of Native American tribes from various geographic regions of the United States.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Describe the impact of immigrants on the Native Americans.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explore ways the daily life of people living in Colonial America changed over time.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Identify reasons people came to the United States throughout history.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Discuss the importance of Ellis Island and the Statue of Liberty to immigration from 1892-1954.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Discuss why immigration continues today.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain the cultural influences and contributions of immigrants today.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Identify terms and designations of time sequence.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: African American History - Positive influences and contributions by African Americans

standards.text: Identify African Americans who demonstrated civic service (i.e., Secretary of State Colin Powell, Civil Air Patrol [CAP] Lt. Willa Beatrice Brown, Carter G. Woodson, Senator Hiram Revels).
standards.label: A

standards.text: Identify oral traditions and folktales of African Americans (e.g., Anansi the Spider, Tale of the Midnight Goat Thief).
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Civics and Government - Foundations of Government, Law, and the American Political System

standards.text: Explain why people form governments.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain how the U.S. government protects the liberty and rights of American citizens.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Civics and Government - Civic and Political Participation

standards.text: Explain what it means to be a U.S. citizen.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Describe the characteristics of responsible citizenship at the local and state levels.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain how citizens demonstrate patriotism.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Recognize symbols, individuals, and documents that represent the United States.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Recognize symbols, individuals, and documents that represent Florida.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Civics and Government - Structure and Functions of Government

standards.text: Identify the Constitution of the United States as the supreme law of the land.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Recognize that people make choices because of limited resources.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Recognize that people supply goods and services based on consumer demands.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Recognize that the United States trades with other nations to exchange goods and services.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain the personal benefits and costs involved in saving and spending.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Geography - The World in Spatial Terms

standards.text: Use different types of maps (political, physical, and thematic) to identify map elements.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Using maps and globes, locate the student’s hometown, Florida, North America, and both the state and national capitals.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Label on a map or globe the continents, oceans, Equator, Prime Meridian, North and South Poles.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Use a map to locate the countries in North America (Canada, United States, Mexico, and the Caribbean Islands).
standards.label: A

key_learning_outcomes.label: C
items: Students examine primary and secondary sources and describe Native American and immigrant history in North America and the United States.
Students identify African Americans who demonstrated civic service and African American oral traditions and folktales named in the benchmarks.
Students explain why people form governments, U.S. citizenship, patriotism, and symbols and documents of the United States and Florida.
Students recognize limited resources, supply and consumer demand, U.S. trade, and benefits and costs of saving and spending.
Students use maps and globes to locate their hometown, Florida, North America, continents, oceans, the Equator, the Prime Meridian, and the poles.
